subject: Defining failover triggers and request for SLA carve-out
messages:
From: Alejandro Ruiz <sre@finovia.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@finovia.com
Date: 2027-05-26T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify failover trigger definitions (RTO/RPO) — potential SLA carve-out

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the call this morning. We're reviewing the draft SLA you sent (v3) and have a specific concern around the conditions that constitute a regional failover. Finovia requires clear, deterministic failover triggers so our ops teams can automate cutover without ambiguous human judgment.

Our ask: can Redwood accept a narrow carve-out where warm-standby activation initiated by the customer (via our automation) does not count against the SLA uptime window if activation was caused by customer-side network isolation or a third-party transit provider failure? We want to avoid a situation where our own network misconfig triggers Redwood's failover SLO and exposes us to penalties.

Relevant points:
- Example scenario included in the attached diagram where traffic is blackholed to the primary region but our control plane remains reachable.
- Proposed carve-out timeline: customer-initiated activation = 72-hour remediation window for SLA credit eligibility review.

Can you confirm whether Redwood would accept: (1) a limited exclusion for customer-initiated failovers originating from customer networking; and (2) language that ties RTO/RPO obligations to Redwood-side confirmed outage?

Alejandro
SRE Lead, Finovia

Attachments: redwood-failover-diagram.png
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alejandro Ruiz <sre@finovia.com>
Cc: procurement@finovia.com, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-26T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify failover trigger definitions (RTO/RPO) — potential SLA carve-out

Alejandro,

Appreciate the clear scenarios and the diagram — helpful. Short answer: we can negotiate careful carve-outs, but the language needs to be precise so it can't be used to avoid operational responsibility when Redwood infrastructure is implicated.

High-level thoughts:
- We are open to a clause that excludes customer-initiated activations when telemetry shows no degraded service from our side (e.g., API control plane health, serving runtime health, and inter-region replication intact).
- We need a deterministic verification step: either automated telemetry signals or a joint post-incident review within 14 days.
- For your proposed 72-hour remediation window, we can accept a provisional 72-hour review period for SLA credit eligibility, but credits would only be applied after an RCA establishes root cause.

I'll loop in Karthik on finer legal/contract language. Can we also get the specific list of telemetry KPIs you expect Redwood to publish for confirmation? That will speed the verification flow.

Thanks — sending a redline proposal back to procurement by early next week.

—Marissa
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Attachment: SLA-DRAFT_v3.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Alejandro Ruiz <sre@finovia.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-27T08:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify failover trigger definitions (RTO/RPO) — potential SLA carve-out

On Thu, May 27, 2027 at 08:46 AM Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com> wrote:
> Alejandro,
>
> Appreciate the clear scenarios and the diagram — helpful. Short answer: we can negotiate careful carve-outs...

Alejandro — quick technical/legal note from our side: we can accept a \"customer-initiated activation\" carve-out if all of the following are true:
1) Customer's automation triggers the warm-standby via an authenticated API call (we log the request and can trace it).
2) Redwood telemetry for the primary region indicates normal serving runtime and control-plane health (we will publish a small set of signals: API-latency-95, KV-cache-hit-rate, inter-region replication lag, control-plane-heartbeat).
3) The customer acknowledges and documents the automation flow in the runbook we store in the contract appendix (so activations are auditable).

If any of the telemetry signals show degradation on Redwood's side within a 15-minute window before the activation, we cannot treat it as a customer-only carve-out. Also: RPO/RTO obligations still apply to our replicated KV and persisted state; we can provide maximum RPO guaranteed for data stored in our managed replication path, with exceptions documented for customer-managed encryption or customer-side replication.

I'll propose specific contract language that enumerates the telemetry set and the log format. Evelyn — can you confirm whether 14 days for post-incident RCA is acceptable from Legal/Compliance?

—Karthik
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Alejandro Ruiz <sre@finovia.com>
Date: 2027-05-28T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify failover trigger definitions (RTO/RPO) — potential SLA carve-out

Marissa / Karthik — 14 days for an RCA is acceptable. A couple of compliance caveats:

- We need to ensure any telemetry we publish for verification does not leak customer PII or secrets. We'll publish aggregated service health metrics and signed attestations for control-plane heartbeats.
- For the carve-out, procurement language must require Finovia to supply automation runbook excerpts and the API call audit trail as part of the review. Without auditable evidence, we can't grant credit.
- We recommend adding an \"escalation / joint-investigation\" clause that triggers a neutral third-party arbiter if Finovia disputes the RCA conclusion within 30 days.

We're ready to produce a redline that: (a) lists the telemetry signals; (b) defines the exact log/audit format; and (c) sets the post-incident timeline (72hr provisional review, 14-day RCA, 30-day dispute window).

Evelyn
Head of Compliance, Redwood Inference
From: Alejandro Ruiz <sre@finovia.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@finovia.com
Date: 2027-06-02T16:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify failover trigger definitions (RTO/RPO) — potential SLA carve-out

Thanks team — this direction looks workable. A couple follow-ups before procurement signs: 

1) Could Redwood publish the telemetry schema (field names, units, and acceptable ranges) so our ops automation can programmatically evaluate whether the signals indicate "Redwood-side degradation"?
2) For the 72-hour provisional review window — if we provide the API audit and runbook excerpts within 24 hours of activation, will Redwood commit to an expedited provisional acceptance so we can avoid unnecessary failback churn?

If we can get those two items in the redline, procurement is comfortable moving forward. Happy to schedule a 30-minute working session next week to finalize the language.

Alejandro
SRE Lead, Finovia
